subject: occupancy using categorical predictor with 0 observations category

messages.author: 61b3b0187be32166
messages.subject: occupancy using categorical predictor with 0 observations category
parts:
Hello everyone,


I have trouble understanding why unmarked is giving me incorrect results when I use categorical predictors.

I collected data on elephant presence on 3 natural reserves which are managed differently. I am trying to predict elephant occupancy using a multivariate model with function occu(). Most of my variables are continuous except for variables “Reserve management” and “Habitat” that are categorical.

The data shows 0 observations at reserve 1, 40 observations at reserve 2 and 7 observations at reserve 3. You don’t need to be statistician to realize that elephants are almost absent in reserve 1 and 3, however these are the results I get when I use only this variable as predictor:



rsrv=occu(~Camera.type~Nom.Reserve,Eleph)
rsrv

 

Call:
occu(formula = ~Camera.type ~ Reserve, data = Eleph)
 
Occupancy:
                  Estimate       SE       z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)         -1.69    0.335 -5.0408 4.63e-07
Reserve1            -17.46 1398.101 -0.0125 9.90e-01
Reserve3             -1.68    0.657 -2.5543 1.06e-02
 
Detection:
                     Estimate    SE     z  P(>|z|)
(Intercept)            -2.418 0.277 -8.73 2.66e-18
Camera.typeCuddeback   -0.686 0.654 -1.05 2.95e-01
 
AIC: 320.9485 
 
 

This shows that there is a significant difference between reserve 2 and 3 (p=0.01) (so far so good) but no difference between reserve 2 and 1 (p=0.99) even though reserve 1 has no observations. Also the SE for reserve1 is ridiculously high.


I guess that unmarked doesn’t like categories where observations are 0 or close to 0 but how could I fix this problem knowing that I want to show that there is a difference in occupancy for elephant even when other factors like distance to water or distance to village are controlled?


Thanks a lot in advance!


Gabriel Valdez

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] occupancy using categorical predictor with 0 observations category
parts:
Tranquilo, hombre,

unmarked is doing exactly the right thing. The estimate of occupancy in the reserve where no elephants were observed is plogis(-17), which is essentially zero. For such a boundary estimate (i.e., 0 or 1 for a probabillity) you can't estimate the standard error numerically, hence, the huge number which you should not interpret (incl. the p-value).

Best regards --  Marc

Gabriel,
 
I think the problem that you describe is known as complete data separation. It's a tricky problem. I have no solution.
https://stats.idre.ucla.edu/other/mult-pkg/faq/general/faqwhat-is-complete-or-quasi-complete-separation-in-logisticprobit-regression-and-how-do-we-deal-with-them/
 
Best wishes, Beni

parts:
Dear Beni,

I am not convinced, to be honest. Complete separation denotes the case where in a logistic regression and in a continuous covariate X, all the covariate values associated with, say, the 0 response are strictly smaller or larger than the covariate values associated with the 1 response.

But Gabriel has no problem at all.

Regards  ---- Marc

Muchas gracias to both of you!

I am amazed at the speed you answered.

Indeed if you do plogis(estimate) you get a value close to 0 and if i predict occupancy based only on this variable I get a predicted value close to 0 although a with confidence interval going from 0 to 1. I think i can still conclude that there is an important difference between the reserves.

From now on i will be more carefull with interpretation.

Thank you and best regards

Gabriel
